672: typedef struct {
673:     /* XADD options */
674:     streamID id; /* User-provided ID, for XADD only. */
675:     int id_given; /* Was an ID different than "*" specified? for XADD only. */
676:     int seq_given; /* Was an ID different than "ms-*" specified? for XADD only. */
677:     int no_mkstream; /* if set to 1 do not create new stream */
678: 
679:     /* XADD + XTRIM common options */
680:     int trim_strategy; /* TRIM_STRATEGY_* */
681:     int trim_strategy_arg_idx; /* Index of the count in MAXLEN/MINID, for rewriting. */
682:     int approx_trim; /* If 1 only delete whole radix tree nodes, so
683:                       * the trim argument is not applied verbatim. */
684:     long long limit; /* Maximum amount of entries to trim. If 0, no limitation
685:                       * on the amount of trimming work is enforced. */
686:     /* TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN options */
687:     long long maxlen; /* After trimming, leave stream at this length . */
688:     /* TRIM_STRATEGY_MINID options */
689:     streamID minid; /* Trim by ID (No stream entries with ID < 'minid' will remain) */
690: } streamAddTrimArgs;
691: 
692: #define TRIM_STRATEGY_NONE 0
693: #define TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN 1
694: #define TRIM_STRATEGY_MINID 2
695: 
696: /* Trim the stream 's' according to args->trim_strategy, and return the
697:  * number of elements removed from the stream. The 'approx' option, if non-zero,
698:  * specifies that the trimming must be performed in a approximated way in
699:  * order to maximize performances. This means that the stream may contain
700:  * entries with IDs < 'id' in case of MINID (or more elements than 'maxlen'
701:  * in case of MAXLEN), and elements are only removed if we can remove
702:  * a *whole* node of the radix tree. The elements are removed from the head
703:  * of the stream (older elements).
704:  *
705:  * The function may return zero if:
706:  *
707:  * 1) The minimal entry ID of the stream is already < 'id' (MINID); or
708:  * 2) The stream is already shorter or equal to the specified max length (MAXLEN); or
709:  * 3) The 'approx' option is true and the head node did not have enough elements
710:  *    to be deleted.
711:  *
712:  * args->limit is the maximum number of entries to delete. The purpose is to
713:  * prevent this function from taking to long.
714:  * If 'limit' is 0 then we do not limit the number of deleted entries.
715:  * Much like the 'approx', if 'limit' is smaller than the number of entries
716:  * that should be trimmed, there is a chance we will still have entries with
717:  * IDs < 'id' (or number of elements >= maxlen in case of MAXLEN).
718:  */
719: int64_t streamTrim(rax *rt, stream *s, streamAddTrimArgs *args) {
720:     size_t maxlen = args->maxlen;
721:     streamID *id = &args->minid;
722:     int approx = args->approx_trim;
723:     int64_t limit = args->limit;
724:     int trim_strategy = args->trim_strategy;
725: 
726:     if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_NONE || rt->numele == 0)
727:         return 0;
728: 
729:     raxIterator ri;
730:     raxStart(&ri,rt);
731:     raxSeek(&ri,"^",NULL,0);
732: 
733:     int64_t deleted = 0;
734:     while (raxNext(&ri)) {
735:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN && s->length <= maxlen)
736:             break;
737: 
738:         unsigned char *lp = ri.data, *p = lpFirst(lp);
739:         listpackEntry header_entry;
740:         unsigned int header_slen;
741:         unsigned char *header_str = lpGetValue(p, &header_slen, &header_entry.lval);
742:         int64_t entries;
743:         if (header_str == NULL) {
744:             entries = header_entry.lval;
745:         } else {
746:             long long header_ll;
747:             int header_ret = string2ll((char*)header_str, header_slen, &header_ll);
748:             serverAssert(header_ret != 0);
749:             entries = header_ll;
750:         }
751: 
752:         /* Check if we exceeded the amount of work we could do */
753:         if (limit && (deleted + entries) > limit)
754:             break;
755: 
756:         /* Check if we can remove the whole node. */
757:         int remove_node;
758:         streamID master_id = {0}; /* For MINID */
759:         if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN) {
760:             remove_node = s->length - entries >= maxlen;
761:         } else {
762:             /* Read the master ID from the radix tree key. */
763:             streamDecodeID(ri.key, &master_id);
764: 
765:             /* Read last ID. */
766:             streamID last_id;
767:             lpGetEdgeStreamID(lp, 0, &master_id, &last_id);
768: 
769:             /* We can remove the entire node id its last ID < 'id' */
770:             remove_node = streamCompareID(&last_id, id) < 0;
771:         }
772: 
773:         if (remove_node) {
774:             lpFree(lp);
775:             raxRemove(rt,ri.key,ri.key_len,NULL);
776:             raxSeek(&ri,">=",ri.key,ri.key_len);
777:             s->length -= entries;
778:             deleted += entries;
779:             continue;
780:         }
781: 
782:         /* If we cannot remove a whole element, and approx is true,
783:          * stop here. */
784:         if (approx) break;
785: 
786:         /* Now we have to trim entries from within 'lp' */
787:         int64_t deleted_from_lp = 0;
788: 
789:         p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip deleted field. */
790:         p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip num-of-fields in the master entry. */
791: 
792:         /* Skip all the master fields. */
793:         int64_t master_fields_count = lpGetInteger(p);
794:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the first field. */
795:         for (int64_t j = 0; j < master_fields_count; j++)
796:             p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip all master fields. */
797:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the zero master entry terminator. */
798: 
799:         /* 'p' is now pointing to the first entry inside the listpack.
800:          * We have to run entry after entry, marking entries as deleted
801:          * if they are already not deleted. */
802:         while (p) {
803:             /* We keep a copy of p (which point to flags part) in order to
804:              * update it after (and if) we actually remove the entry */
805:             unsigned char *pcopy = p;
806: 
807:             int flags = lpGetInteger(p);
808:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip flags. */
809:             int to_skip;
810: 
811:             int ms_delta = lpGetInteger(p);
812:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip ID ms delta */
813:             int seq_delta = lpGetInteger(p);
814:             p = lpNext(lp, p); /* Skip ID seq delta */
815: 
816:             streamID currid = {0}; /* For MINID */
817:             if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MINID) {
818:                 currid.ms = master_id.ms + ms_delta;
819:                 currid.seq = master_id.seq + seq_delta;
820:             }
821: 
822:             int stop;
823:             if (trim_strategy == TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN) {
824:                 stop = s->length <= maxlen;
825:             } else {
826:                 /* Following IDs will definitely be greater because the rax
827:                  * tree is sorted, no point of continuing. */
828:                 stop = streamCompareID(&currid, id) >= 0;
829:             }
830:             if (stop)
831:                 break;
832: 
833:             if (flags & STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_SAMEFIELDS) {
834:                 to_skip = master_fields_count;
835:             } else {
836:                 to_skip = lpGetInteger(p); /* Get num-fields. */
837:                 p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip num-fields. */
838:                 to_skip *= 2; /* Fields and values. */
839:             }
840: 
841:             while(to_skip--) p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the whole entry. */
842:             p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip the final lp-count field. */
843: 
844:             /* Mark the entry as deleted. */
845:             if (!(flags & STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_DELETED)) {
846:                 intptr_t delta = p - lp;
847:                 flags |= STREAM_ITEM_FLAG_DELETED;
848:                 lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp, &pcopy, flags);
849:                 deleted_from_lp++;
850:                 s->length--;
851:                 p = lp + delta;
852:             }
853:         }
854:         deleted += deleted_from_lp;
855: 
856:         /* Now we the entries/deleted counters. */
857:         p = lpFirst(lp);
858:         lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp,&p,entries-deleted_from_lp);
859:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip deleted field. */
860:         int64_t marked_deleted = lpGetInteger(p);
861:         lp = lpReplaceInteger(lp,&p,marked_deleted+deleted_from_lp);
862:         p = lpNext(lp,p); /* Skip num-of-fields in the master entry. */
863: 
864:         /* Here we should perform garbage collection in case at this point
865:          * there are too many entries deleted inside the listpack. */
866:         entries -= deleted_from_lp;
867:         marked_deleted += deleted_from_lp;
868:         if (entries + marked_deleted > 10 && marked_deleted > entries/2) {
869:             /* TODO: perform a garbage collection. */
870:         }
871: 
872:         /* Update the listpack with the new pointer. */
873:         raxInsert(rt,ri.key,ri.key_len,lp,NULL);
874: 
875:         break; /* If we are here, there was enough to delete in the current
876:                   node, so no need to go to the next node. */
877:     }
878: 
879:     raxStop(&ri);
880:     return deleted;
881: }
882: 
883: /* Trims a stream by length. Returns the number of deleted items. */
884: int64_t streamTrimByLength(stream *s, long long maxlen, int approx) {
885:     streamAddTrimArgs args = {
886:         .trim_strategy = TRIM_STRATEGY_MAXLEN,
887:         .approx_trim = approx,
888:         .limit = approx ? 100 * server.stream_node_max_entries : 0,
889:         .maxlen = maxlen
890:     };
891:     return streamTrim(s->rax, s, &args);
892: }

250: /* This is a wrapper function for lpGet() to directly get an integer value
251:  * from the listpack (that may store numbers as a string), converting
252:  * the string if needed.
253:  * The 'valid" argument is an optional output parameter to get an indication
254:  * if the record was valid, when this parameter is NULL, the function will
255:  * fail with an assertion. */
256: static inline int64_t lpGetIntegerIfValid(unsigned char *ele, int *valid) {
257:     int64_t v;
258:     unsigned char *e = lpGet(ele,&v,NULL);
259:     if (e == NULL) {
260:         if (valid)
261:             *valid = 1;
262:         return v;
263:     }
264:     /* The following code path should never be used for how listpacks work:
265:      * they should always be able to store an int64_t value in integer
266:      * encoded form. However the implementation may change. */
267:     long long ll;
268:     int ret = string2ll((char*)e,v,&ll);
269:     if (valid)
270:         *valid = ret;
271:     else
272:         serverAssert(ret != 0);
273:     v = ll;
274:     return v;
275: }
276: 
277: #define lpGetInteger(ele) lpGetIntegerIfValid(ele, NULL)
278: 
279: /* Get an edge streamID of a given listpack.
280:  * 'master_id' is an input param, used to build the 'edge_id' output param */
281: int lpGetEdgeStreamID(unsigned char *lp, int first, streamID *master_id, streamID *edge_id)
282: {
283:    if (lp == NULL)
284:        return 0;
285: 
286:    unsigned char *lp_ele;
287: 
288:    /* We need to seek either the first or the last entry depending
289:     * on the direction of the iteration. */
290:    if (first) {
291:        /* Get the master fields count. */
292:        lp_ele = lpFirst(lp);        /* Seek items count */
293:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek deleted count. */
294:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek num fields. */
295:        int64_t master_fields_count = lpGetInteger(lp_ele);
296:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek first field. */
297: 
298:        /* If we are iterating in normal order, skip the master fields
299:         * to seek the first actual entry. */
300:        for (int64_t i = 0; i < master_fields_count; i++)
301:            lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele);
302: 
303:        /* If we are going forward, skip the previous entry's
304:         * lp-count field (or in case of the master entry, the zero
305:         * term field) */
306:        lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele);
307:        if (lp_ele == NULL)
308:            return 0;
309:    } else {
310:        /* If we are iterating in reverse direction, just seek the
311:         * last part of the last entry in the listpack (that is, the
312:         * fields count). */
313:        lp_ele = lpLast(lp);
314: 
315:        /* If we are going backward, read the number of elements this
316:         * entry is composed of, and jump backward N times to seek
317:         * its start. */
318:        int64_t lp_count = lpGetInteger(lp_ele);
319:        if (lp_count == 0) /* We reached the master entry. */
320:            return 0;
321: 
322:        while (lp_count--)
323:            lp_ele = lpPrev(lp, lp_ele);
324:    }
325: 
326:    lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele); /* Seek ID (lp_ele currently points to 'flags'). */
327: 
328:    /* Get the ID: it is encoded as difference between the master
329:     * ID and this entry ID. */
330:    streamID id = *master_id;
331:    id.ms += lpGetInteger(lp_ele);
332:    lp_ele = lpNext(lp, lp_ele);
333:    id.seq += lpGetInteger(lp_ele);
334:    *edge_id = id;
335:    return 1;
336: }

351: /* Convert the specified stream entry ID as a 128 bit big endian number, so
352:  * that the IDs can be sorted lexicographically. */
353: void streamEncodeID(void *buf, streamID *id) {
354:     uint64_t e[2];
355:     e[0] = htonu64(id->ms);
356:     e[1] = htonu64(id->seq);
357:     memcpy(buf,e,sizeof(e));
358: }
359: 
360: /* This is the reverse of streamEncodeID(): the decoded ID will be stored
361:  * in the 'id' structure passed by reference. The buffer 'buf' must point
362:  * to a 128 bit big-endian encoded ID. */
363: void streamDecodeID(void *buf, streamID *id) {
364:     uint64_t e[2];
365:     memcpy(e,buf,sizeof(e));
366:     id->ms = ntohu64(e[0]);
367:     id->seq = ntohu64(e[1]);
368: }

370: /* Compare two stream IDs. Return -1 if a < b, 0 if a == b, 1 if a > b. */
371: int streamCompareID(streamID *a, streamID *b) {
372:     if (a->ms > b->ms) return 1;
373:     else if (a->ms < b->ms) return -1;
374:     /* The ms part is the same. Check the sequence part. */
375:     else if (a->seq > b->seq) return 1;
376:     else if (a->seq < b->seq) return -1;
377:     /* Everything is the same: IDs are equal. */
378:     return 0;
379: }

381: void streamGetEdgeID(stream *s, int first, streamID *edge_id)
382: {
383:     raxIterator ri;
384:     raxStart(&ri, s->rax);
385:     int empty;
386:     if (first) {
387:         raxSeek(&ri, "^", NULL, 0);
388:         empty = !raxNext(&ri);
389:     } else {
390:         raxSeek(&ri, "$", NULL, 0);

394:     if (empty) {
395:         /* Stream is empty, mark edge ID as lowest/highest possible. */
396:         edge_id->ms = first ? UINT64_MAX : 0;
397:         edge_id->seq = first ? UINT64_MAX : 0;

399:         return;

401: 
402:     unsigned char *lp = ri.data;
403: 
404:     /* Read the master ID from the radix tree key. */
405:     streamID master_id;

414: /* Adds a new item into the stream 's' having the specified number of
415:  * field-value pairs as specified in 'numfields' and stored into 'argv'.
416:  * Returns the new entry ID populating the 'added_id' structure.
417:  *
418:  * If 'use_id' is not NULL, the ID is not auto-generated by the function,
419:  * but instead the passed ID is used to add the new entry. In this case
420:  * adding the entry may fail as specified later in this comment.
421:  * 
422:  * When 'use_id' is used alongside with a zero 'seq-given', the sequence
423:  * part of the passed ID is ignored and the function will attempt to use an
424:  * auto-generated sequence.
425:  *
426:  * The function returns C_OK if the item was added, this is always true
427:  * if the ID was generated by the function. However the function may return
428:  * C_ERR in several cases:
429:  * 1. If an ID was given via 'use_id', but adding it failed since the
430:  *    current top ID is greater or equal. errno will be set to EDOM.
431:  * 2. If a size of a single element or the sum of the elements is too big to
432:  *    be stored into the stream. errno will be set to ERANGE. */
433: int streamAppendItem(stream *s, robj **argv, int64_t numfields, streamID *added_id, streamID *use_id, int seq_given) {
434: 
435:     /* Generate the new entry ID. */
436:     streamID id;
437:     if (use_id) {
438:         if (seq_given) {
439:             id = *use_id;
440:         } else {
441:             /* The automatically generated sequence can be either zero (new
442:              * timestamps) or the incremented sequence of the last ID. In the
443:              * latter case, we need to prevent an overflow/advancing forward
444:              * in time. */
445:             if (s->last_id.ms == use_id->ms) {
446:                 if (s->last_id.seq == UINT64_MAX) {
447:                     return C_ERR;
448:                 }
449:                 id = s->last_id;
450:                 id.seq++;
451:             } else {
452:                 id = *use_id;
453:             }
454:         }
455:     } else {
456:         streamNextID(&s->last_id,&id);
457:     }
458: 
459:     /* Check that the new ID is greater than the last entry ID
460:      * or return an error. Automatically generated IDs might
461:      * overflow (and wrap-around) when incrementing the sequence
462:        part. */
463:     if (streamCompareID(&id,&s->last_id) <= 0) {
464:         errno = EDOM;
465:         return C_ERR;
466:     }
467: 
468:     /* Avoid overflow when trying to add an element to the stream (listpack
469:      * can only host up to 32bit length sttrings, and also a total listpack size
470:      * can't be bigger than 32bit length. */
471:     size_t totelelen = 0;
472:     for (int64_t i = 0; i < numfields*2; i++) {
473:         sds ele = argv[i]->ptr;
474:         totelelen += sdslen(ele);
475:     }
476:     if (totelelen > STREAM_LISTPACK_MAX_SIZE) {
477:         errno = ERANGE;
478:         return C_ERR;
479:     }
480: 
481:     /* Add the new entry. */
482:     raxIterator ri;
483:     raxStart(&ri,s->rax);
484:     raxSeek(&ri,"$",NULL,0);
485: 
486:     size_t lp_bytes = 0;        /* Total bytes in the tail listpack. */
487:     unsigned char *lp = NULL;   /* Tail listpack pointer. */
488: 
489:     if (!raxEOF(&ri)) {
490:         /* Get a reference to the tail node listpack. */
491:         lp = ri.data;
492:         lp_bytes = lpBytes(lp);
493:     }
494:     raxStop(&ri);
495: 
496:     /* We have to add the key into the radix tree in lexicographic order,
497:      * to do so we consider the ID as a single 128 bit number written in
498:      * big endian, so that the most significant bytes are the first ones. */
499:     uint64_t rax_key[2];    /* Key in the radix tree containing the listpack.*/
500:     streamID master_id;     /* ID of the master entry in the listpack. */
501: 
502:     /* Create a new listpack and radix tree node if needed. Note that when
503:      * a new listpack is created, we populate it with a "master entry". This
504:      * is just a set of fields that is taken as references in order to compress
505:      * the stream entries that we'll add inside the listpack.
506:      *
507:      * Note that while we use the first added entry fields to create
508:      * the master entry, the first added entry is NOT represented in the master
509:      * entry, which is a stand alone object. But of course, the first entry
510:      * will compress well because it's used as reference.
511:      *
512:      * The master entry is composed like in the following example:
513:      *
514:      * +-------+---------+------------+---------+--/--+---------+---------+-+
515:      * | count | deleted | num-fields | field_1 | field_2 | ... | field_N |0|
516:      * +-------+---------+------------+---------+--/--+---------+---------+-+
517:      *
518:      * count and deleted just represent respectively the total number of
519:      * entries inside the listpack that are valid, and marked as deleted
520:      * (deleted flag in the entry flags set). So the total number of items
521:      * actually inside the listpack (both deleted and not) is count+deleted.
522:      *
523:      * The real entries will be encoded with an ID that is just the
524:      * millisecond and sequence difference compared to the key stored at
525:      * the radix tree node containing the listpack (delta encoding), and
526:      * if the fields of the entry are the same as the master entry fields, the
527:      * entry flags will specify this fact and the entry fields and number
528:      * of fields will be omitted (see later in the code of this function).
529:      *
530:      * The "0" entry at the end is the same as the 'lp-count' entry in the
531:      * regular stream entries (see below), and marks the fact that there are
532:      * no more entries, when we scan the stream from right to left. */
533: 
534:     /* First of all, check if we can append to the current macro node or
535:      * if we need to switch to the next one. 'lp' will be set to NULL if
536:      * the current node is full. */
537:     if (lp != NULL) {
538:         size_t node_max_bytes = server.stream_node_max_bytes;
539:         if (node_max_bytes == 0 || node_max_bytes > STREAM_LISTPACK_MAX_SIZE)
540:             node_max_bytes = STREAM_LISTPACK_MAX_SIZE;
